data.gender_notes: Kiriella is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Greek word 'kērillē', meaning 'lamp', 'light' or 'torch'. In Christian tradition, Kiriella may symbolize the illumination of faith or the light of God in one's life. The name Kiriella carries the meaning “Little lamp” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Kiriella usually hope their child will grow to embody little lamp and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Kiriella total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

historical_references.reference: According to local tradition, St. Kiriella, also known as Quirinus or Quirinus of Thessalonica, was a Christian martyr who lived during the Roman Empire. He is believed to have been a bishop in Thessalonica, Greece, and was martyred during the reign of Emperor Galerius in the early 4th century. The exact details of his martyrdom are uncertain, but it is said that he was put to death for refusing to offer sacrifice to the Roman gods.

Another tradition places St. Kiriella as the bishop of Cyrene in Libya during the 3rd century CE. According to this account, he was a prominent figure in the early Christian community and was known for his miraculous healings and exorcisms. He was arrested and brought before the Roman governor during the reign of Emperor Maximinus Thrax for refusing to renounce his faith. After being subjected to various forms of torture, he was eventually put to death.
